newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat continues to rise in near-term contracts.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat continues to rise in near-term contracts.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat continued to rise in near-term contracts on Thursday on concerns about dry weather in southern districts of Australia's eastern states and in South Australia.
May 1997, the nearest contract, added A$1.50 to A$185.00 a tonne on eight lots traded. It was the only contract to change hands.
Settlement prices for May and July 1997 also both advanced by 50 cents to A$1.50, while more distant contracts generally fell by 50 cents to A$1.50.
"The market has been a bit short and there's been a fair bit of buying," one broker said.
The main concern continued to be dry weather in the south and this would dictate whether the market would continue to rise, he said.
New crop wheat futures had not risen as well as the near-term contracts, he noted. "If we get some rain I think it might ease back," he said.
